title: Would you rather work less? You’re not alone
gist: Resolution Foundation's weekly note: the Bank of England's first rate hike in 3+ years (Iran-war energy shock) comes with forecasts of 4.9% peak inflation, target only by Q3 2028 and no real-pay recovery until 2028, overtaking the OBR's rosier Budget view. Also covers limits of public land for housing (Manchester), the Carer's Allowance earnings cliff, Space Race R&D tilting tech toward automation, and BSA data showing every group increasingly wants to work less.

themes.theme: BoE hike and stickier UK inflation

insights.claim: The Bank of England raised interest rates in early November 2026 for the first time in more than three years, with the UK the last G7 member to move in response to the war in Iran.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: UK monetary policy has turned hawkish on an energy/war shock; gilts and sterling now price a tightening cycle.
insights.quote: the UK the last G7 member to move in response to the war in Iran
insights.locator: Something for the weekend | Rate expectations

insights.claim: The Bank of England now forecasts UK inflation peaking at 4.9 per cent in spring 2027 and not returning to target until Q3 2028, two years later than previously planned.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: A two-year delay in reaching target implies higher-for-longer UK rates; watch spring CPI prints versus the 4.9% peak.
insights.quote: not to hit target until Q3 2028, two years later than planned

insights.claim: The Bank of England's inflation path already assumes Bank rate climbs to 5 per cent, meaning even the gloomy inflation forecast is conditional on further tightening.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Market should expect further hikes toward 5%; upside inflation risk would require even more.
insights.quote: a worrying scenario that nonetheless assumes Bank rate will climb to 5 per cent

insights.claim: The OBR's Budget forecasts, built on August energy prices that have since risen sharply, expected UK inflation to stay just under 4 per cent next year, making them already stale versus the Bank's projections.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Official fiscal forecasts understate inflation; fiscal headroom and real-terms spending plans are at risk of revision.
insights.quote: Working from August’s energy prices, which have since risen sharply

insights.claim: Energy prices rising sharply since August are the key driver pushing UK inflation forecasts higher, linking the Iran war energy shock directly to UK living standards.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: UK inflation and consumer outlook are hostage to energy prices; track wholesale gas/oil.

insights.claim: Average UK 2-year fixed mortgage rates have risen 1.2 percentage points since February 2026, costing a typical first-time buyer an extra £140 a month.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Housing demand and housebuilder/mortgage lender volumes face pressure as refinancing costs rise.
insights.quote: Average 2-year fixed rates have risen 1.2 percentage points since February

insights.claim: The Bank of England does not expect UK real pay to rise above its 2025 level until 2028, and relative to previous forecasts the average private-sector worker will earn £670 less next year in real terms.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Weak real incomes point to soft UK consumer discretionary spending through 2027-28.
insights.quote: the average private-sector worker is set to earn £670 less next year in real terms

insights.claim: Resolution Foundation warns that if the Bank of England's inflation path plays out, even the OBR's already meagre forecast of living standards growth for the 2020s could disappear entirely.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: A lost decade for UK living standards raises political pressure for fiscal support and redistribution.
insights.quote: If the Bank’s inflation path plays out, even that could disappear.

insights.claim: Resolution Foundation's chief executive criticised the poor targeting of the Government's winter energy bill support before the Treasury Select Committee, arguing who gets support will remain crucial all winter.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Expect pressure to retarget energy support, with fiscal cost and distributional implications.
insights.quote: my disappointment in the poor targeting of the Government’s energy bill support this winter

insights.claim: Manchester City Council owns roughly a third of the city, but only 63 hectares of that land is idle and suitable for housing, enough for about 4,500 homes.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Public-land housing schemes deliver one-off boosts, not structural supply; housing shortage persists.
insights.quote: only 63 hectares of that is idle and suitable

insights.claim: Building on Manchester's idle public land would house under a quarter of the city's 20,000-plus households on the social housing waiting list, so public land alone cannot solve the housing shortage.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Government housing targets depend on other levers (money, council capacity, private land).
insights.quote: a one-off boost that would house under a quarter of the city’s 20,000-plus households

insights.claim: Resolution Foundation argues re-pegging Local Housing Allowance to actual rents would help private renters immediately while new supply takes time.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: A potential welfare spending lever that would support rental income for landlords/BTR sector.
insights.quote: re-pegging Local Housing Allowance to actual rents would help private renters now

insights.claim: Carer's Allowance pays nearly £87 a week but is withdrawn entirely once earnings exceed £204 a week, creating a cliff edge.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Cliff-edge benefit design suppresses labour supply among carers.
insights.quote: Carer’s Allowance provides nearly £87 a week, but earning above £204 a week wipes it out entirely

insights.claim: After crossing the Carer's Allowance earnings cliff, former claimants are 6.2 percentage points more likely to be behind on rent or mortgage and 7.2 points more likely to struggle to get by, driven by nine fewer working hours a week and £592 a month lower earnings rather than extra caring.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Shows benefit design distorts work hours; reform could lift labour participation.
insights.quote: nine fewer hours a week and £592 a month less

insights.claim: The Government's planned £1-for-£1 taper for Carer's Allowance would turn the earnings cliff into a plateau, a change Resolution Foundation calls welcome but long overdue.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Watch implementation as a modest positive for carer labour supply.
insights.quote: The Government’s planned £1-for-£1 taper turns the cliff into a plateau

insights.claim: NASA-sponsored patents during the Space Race were more likely to be automation-oriented than others (71 per cent versus 55 per cent), because NASA's mission was getting machines to work where humans could not survive.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Public R&D missions shape the direction of technology, not just its pace.
insights.quote: NASA-sponsored patents were more likely to be automation-oriented than others (71 per cent versus 55 per cent)

insights.claim: In industries and places most exposed to the Space Race, manufacturers' labour share fell by around a quarter relative to the rest of manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Mission-driven tech funding can shift income from labour to capital.
insights.quote: manufacturers’ labour share fell by around a quarter relative to the rest of manufacturing

insights.claim: With governments including the UK now backing AI and defence missions, what they choose to fund, not just how much, could shape the impact of technology on workers' labour share.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: State AI/defence spending may accelerate automation and capital-share gains; a second-order labour-market risk.
insights.quote: what they choose to fund, not just how much, could shape the impact on workers

themes.theme: Shifting work preferences and job quality

insights.claim: British Social Attitudes data show that by 2025 every demographic group had more people in full-time work than wanted to be, and every group increasingly wishes to work less than a decade earlier.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Secular decline in desired hours may constrain UK labour supply and push demand for flexible/part-time roles.
insights.quote: every group increasingly wishes they were working less than they are

insights.claim: Over the last decade men under 50 flipped from more wanting full-time work than having it to more having it than wanting it, with the steepest rise among men aged 30-49 and the biggest rise in part-time preference among childless men, not fathers.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: The shift is not explained by childcare; points to broader attitudinal change in male labour supply.
insights.quote: childless men saw the biggest rise in preference for part-time work

insights.claim: Andrew Harrop's Work that Matters survey of over 4,000 UK workers on 40 job-quality measures found care staff did significantly better than other low-to-middle-paid workers on nine measures and worse on none, and were the most confident of any sector their job will exist in 10-20 years.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Care work perceived as automation-proof and secure; labour supply to the sector less fragile than assumed.
insights.quote: care staff did significantly better than other low

insights.claim: Care workers' strong attachment to meaningful work can lead them to tolerate poor pay and conditions, including illegal underpayment, which the sector should not exploit.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Regulatory/wage pressure risk for care providers if underpayment is addressed.
insights.quote: that attachment can lead workers to tolerate poor pay and conditions, including illegal underpayment
